gaps.hint: to his credit = in his favour
gaps.explanation: 'to somebody's credit' — something in their favour.

gaps.sentence: The two reports differ ___ several important respects.
The smell was ___ this world — absolutely incredible.
She resigned ___ the grounds of ill health.
gaps.explanation: 'on the grounds of' = for the reason of.

gaps.sentence: She's ___ charge of the whole marketing department.
The negotiations broke down ___ the very brink of success.
gaps.explanation: 'on the brink of' = on the point of.

gaps.sentence: I did it ___ my own initiative — nobody asked me.
gaps.explanation: 'of one's own initiative' = without being asked.
